articles.title: C. J. Stroud and the Texans are at odds over the player's demand for a $70,000,000 contract
articles.standfirst: Stroud’s $70 million contract hopes create high-stakes dilemma for Texans
articles.summary: Stroud’s $70 million contract hopes create high-stakes dilemma for Texans
articles.body:
C.J. Stroud’s future with the Houston Texans has emerged as one of the NFL’s most intriguing contract storylines, with the two sides reportedly discussing an extension while remaining far apart on a potential agreement.

ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter provided an update Thursday, revealing that Houston has held discussions with its starting quarterback about a new deal.

However, Schefter indicated that the negotiations aren’t close to completion and could continue into the regular season.

"The Houston Texans have had discussions with CJ Stroud about a new deal. My understanding is they’re not close at this particular time. Talks will continue. We’ll see if they’re able to get anything done by the time the season begins, or shortly thereafter,” Schefter said on NFL Live.

The timing could be crucial for both sides. Stroud remains under contract through 2027 after the Texans exercised his fifth-year option earlier this year. That gives Houston significant control over his future while also providing the team with time to evaluate whether he’s worthy of a massive long-term commitment.

Waiting could carry its own risks for Stroud . If he produces a spectacular 2026 campaign, his value could rise considerably, particularly with several other young quarterbacks expected to enter extension negotiations following the season.

The reported $70 million annual figure surrounding Stroud would put him among the highest-paid quarterbacks in league history. However, there hasn’t been official confirmation that this is a firm demand from Stroud or his representatives.

Texans must decide how much C.J. Stroud is worth

Houston has plenty to consider before committing that kind of money. Stroud won Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2023 after leading the Texans to the playoffs and quickly establishing himself as the franchise’s quarterback. Since then, however, his performance has been less consistent.

His struggles were particularly evident during Houston’s playoff defeat last season, when he threw five interceptions and lost two fumbles across two postseason starts.

Those performances have contributed to questions about whether he’s still on track to become the elite quarterback many expected him to be after his remarkable rookie campaign.

At the same time, the Texans haven’t indicated that they’ve given up on Stroud . Team owner Cal McNair has publicly expressed his commitment to the quarterback, while the organization continues to work toward finding a long-term solution.

Houston has also demonstrated that it’s prepared to reward its young stars. The Texans recently signed defensive end Will Anderson Jr., who was selected one pick after Stroud in the 2023 draft, to a three-year extension worth $150 million. That deal reportedly made Anderson the highest-paid defensive end in NFL history.

That could add another layer of pressure to Stroud’s situation. As teammate after teammate secures long-term financial security, questions about when the Texans will do the same for their quarterback will likely become louder.

The decision ultimately comes down to risk for Houston. If Stroud thrives in 2026, waiting could make his next contract dramatically more expensive. If he struggles again, the Texans may feel justified in delaying or reconsidering a massive commitment.

articles.title: CJ Stroud’s viral warmup was done by Aryna Sabalenka: What it is and how it benefits athletes
articles.standfirst: The Houston Texans quarterback surprised many with an eye and thumb dominated workout during his warmup routine before a preseason game.
articles.summary: The Houston Texans quarterback surprised many with an eye and thumb dominated workout during his warmup routine before a preseason game.
articles.body:
Despite being just 24 years old and having a a Pro Bowl season under his belt, CJ Stroud heads into the 2026 NFL season as one of the most scrutinized players in the league. After an implosion in last year’s playoffs, all eyes are on the young quarterback in his fourth season.

That includes the preseason, as Stroud got some snaps in the Houston Texans ’ second preseason contest against the Las Vegas Raiders on Thursday night. Stroud didn’t play much, but he ended up going viral on social media anyway. That was thanks to a warmup exercise that caught the attention of fans all across the internet.

CJ Stroud’s eye-thumb exercise was viralized by Aryna Sabalenka months ago

During the warmup, Stroud holds out his thumbs and alternates looking at each of them with both eyes very quickly . First he does it with his arms extended out, then one on top and one on the bottom. While it might seem weird to football fans, it’s not uncommon among professional athletes .

Not long ago, a clip of tennis superstar Aryna Sabalenka doing a very similar eye drill went viral on social media. Sabalenka practically did the same eye movements Stroud did, but with tennis balls instead of thumbs moving around. This type of drill can help as a neural system warmup as well as an exercise to strengthen eye muscles .

It makes sense that a quarterback would be the one doing that type of drill, as it’s a position that requires an incredible amount of split-second mental processing , through the eyes to the brain. Football players likely work on these types of exercises behind closed doors, but it’s rarely seen on the field during warmups.

Stroud bringing the exercise into the national spotlight could very well lead to more quarterbacks incorporating it into their warmup routines, possibly as soon as this season.

articles.title: Derek Stingley Jr.’s $150K diamond chain breaks in freak sideline accident during Texans game
articles.standfirst: The Texans star’s attempt to control a football suddenly turned into a very expensive mistake
articles.summary: The Texans star’s attempt to control a football suddenly turned into a very expensive mistake
articles.body:
Derek Stingley Jr. wasn't even playing when one of the most expensive moments of the Houston Texans ' preseason unfolded on the sideline

The star cornerback was standing casually with a cup of Gatorade when a football suddenly came toward him. With one hand occupied, Stingley tried to control it against his chest only for the ball to apparently strike the large diamond pendant hanging from his neck. The pendant immediately fell to the ground.

Stingley's reaction somehow made the scene even better. He simply looked down with a completely serious expression, processed what had happened and calmly picked up the pendant. The chain has reportedly been valued at around $150,000 , turning an innocent attempt to catch a football into a painfully expensive-looking accident.

Derek Stingley Jr. can certainly afford expensive jewelry

Fortunately for Stingley, $150,000 represents a very different kind of expense than it would for most people. Houston signed him to a three-year, $90 million extension in 2025, including $89 million guaranteed. At the time, the $30 million annual value made him the highest-paid defensive back in NFL history.

And the Texans didn't give him that money based on potential alone. The former No. 3 overall pick has developed into one of the NFL's elite cornerbacks.

After recording five interceptions in both 2023 and 2024, Stingley added four more in 2025, including his first career interception returned for a touchdown.

He now has 15 interceptions through his first four NFL seasons and earned first-team All-Pro honors in each of the last two.

So the viral scene offered a very different look at one of Houston's biggest stars.

Stingley usually makes his money preventing footballs from reaching their intended target; this time, one found him while he was simply standing on the sideline and somehow managed to hit what may have been the most expensive possible target.

articles.title: "Bigger Than Football" - Fans divided as Azeez Al-Shaair risks substantial fines for political gear
articles.standfirst: The Houston Texans linebacker has again used his platform to highlight Hind Rajab.
articles.summary: The Houston Texans linebacker has again used his platform to highlight Hind Rajab.
articles.body:
Azeez Al-Shaair has again used his NFL platform to highlight the death of Hind Rajab , and the Houston Texans linebacker is now facing another league fine after the message appeared on his eye black.

The NFL fined Al-Shaair $11,492 for displaying “Hind Rajab” during Houston ’s Week 1 loss to the Buffalo Bills . The penalty concerns an unauthorized personal message under league equipment rules.

Rajab was five when she was killed in Gaza City in January 2024 after the car carrying her family came under fire. Her death drew international attention after she remained trapped and called for help.

Al-Shaair has previously faced the NFL ’s discipline for a similar message. He was fined $11,593 in January after displaying “stop the genocide” on his eye black during a playoff win over the Pittsburgh Steelers .

At the time, Al-Shaair explained why he accepted the possibility of another penalty while arguing that the subject was bigger than football and that he wanted people to consider the suffering of civilians.

“I knew that that was a fine,” Al-Shaair said. “I understood what I was doing. But I was told that if I wore that in the game I would be pulled out the game, so I think that was probably the part I was confused about.

“At the end of the day, it’s bigger than me. The things that are going through makes people uncomfortable, imagine how (Palestinians) feel? That’s the biggest thing. I have no affiliation, no connection, to these people.

“Other than the fact that I am a human being. If you have a heart and you’re a human being, and you see what’s going on in this world, you check yourself real quick."

The death of Rajab became a global symbol of the Gaza war’s civilian toll. More than two years later, Israel ’s military has acknowledged that its troops fired on the car carrying her family and ordered a criminal investigation.

The admission marks a major development in a case that drew global attention after Hind was trapped inside the vehicle, surrounded by dead relatives, while pleading with Palestinian medics to come and save her.

Israeli officials had previously said troops were not present near the vehicle. Investigations by The Washington Post and Sky News later found evidence indicating Israeli armored forces were in the area.

Now, the military says its review found that Israeli troops fired at the vehicle as it approached them. It also said the case would be examined by the Military Police Criminal Investigation Division.

On January 29, 2024, Hind and six relatives were trying to flee Gaza City in a black Kia when the vehicle came under fire.

Layan called the Palestine Red Crescent Society and told dispatchers, “They are shooting at us. The tank is right next to me.” Layan was then killed as gunfire erupted around the vehicle. When responders called back, Hind answered and said the others were dead, while warning that the tank was still approaching. Hind remained on the phone with Red Crescent dispatchers for hours. “I’m so scared, please come. Come take me. Please, will you come?” The Red Crescent coordinated with Palestinian health officials and the Israeli military before sending an ambulance toward the vehicle. Contact was eventually lost after reports of gunfire or an explosion. Twelve days later, the bodies were recovered after Israeli forces withdrew from the area. Hind was found inside the bullet-riddled car, while the ambulance was discovered nearby, destroyed. The two paramedics sent to rescue her, Yusuf al-Zeino and Ahmed al-Madhoun , were also found dead. Their deaths became part of the wider international scrutiny surrounding the incident.

articles.title: The NFL fines a Azeez Al-Shaair for wearing the name of a Palestinian girl killed by Israel
articles.standfirst: Azeez Al-Shaair of the Houston Texans will have to pay $11,492 for displaying the name of Hind Rajab, the 5-year-old girl killed by Israel whose story made it to the Oscars
articles.summary: Azeez Al-Shaair of the Houston Texans will have to pay $11,492 for displaying the name of Hind Rajab, the 5-year-old girl killed by Israel whose story made it to the Oscars
articles.body:
NFL player Azeez Al-Shaair was fined more than $11,000 for displaying the name of a Palestinian girl killed by Israeli forces on a face strip, during the game in which his team, the Houston Texans, faced the Buffalo Bills.

The player had written "Hind Rajab" on that black paint, the name of the five-year-old girl whose murder in Gaza in 2024, after Israeli troops fired at her family's disabled car, was the subject of a documentary that is nominated for the Oscars.

According to NFL regulations, displaying personal messages of any kind, including political statements, is prohibited, during games. Thus, an NFL spokesperson confirmed that the fine imposed on Azeez Al-Shaair amounted to $11,941 for that infraction.

It is not the first time that 29-year-old Al-Shaair has spoken out about the situation in Gaza. "I feel like it’s something they’re trying to silence," he told the "Houston Chronicle" in 2024. Al-Shaair received a similar fine in January for displaying the message "stop the genocide".

Kyrie Irving offered to pay the fine

Other athletes, such as Dallas Mavericks player Kyrie Irving, showed their support for Al-Shaair and offered to personally pay the football player's fine . "I'll cover his fine," Irving posted on social media.

Irving has also been a prominent figure in the public demonstration of support for Palestinians, posting on social media about the needs of Palestinian children and wearing T-shirts in tribute to the journalists killed in Gaza.
